scope: Read-only proposed two-case genuine preference fork lifecycle; no parent implementation approval
verdict: Supported direction with concrete integration constraints below; no chain operations performed

constraints.detail: Installed Sequencer.pause gracefully drains work and pending L1 requests, but existing drainT04Checkpoints finally restarts it. Do not use return from that helper as proof of pause. After final pause, require fresh proposed==checkpointed and actual rollup pending checkpoint equality before retaining L1 ancestor and L2 snapshot. Keep sole miner alive until graceful pause/drain completes, then join it and read back restored controls.

Stop empty-checkpoint scope, drain, sync PXE and inspect the actual original signed Tx anchor hash/height equals selected disposable X; merely observing an earlier PXE header does not bind the later proof. R must retain all funding/collateral/FPC/Bok/root prerequisites and, in marker case, initialized bookmark head. Check proven/finalized floors at R before mutation.

Pool handlePrunedBlocks unmines and revalidates metadata with BlockHeader/DoubleSpend validators against syncImmediate committed world state. Mined entries normally have no protection entry. Natural missing-anchor dropping while sequencer paused is supported, but receipt builder reports pending while P2P still knows a transaction after archiver prunes it. Require real dropped receipt, default isValidTx invalid with only Block header not found, and second dropped receipt; pending/unknown remain fenced, no pool deletes or forced policy.

Native L1 pending checkpoint==R is insufficient. Wait for archiver canonical R, world-state committed R and normal PXE.sync rollback. PXE rolls back its stores atomically before advancing tip cursor; do not touch caches or replace node responses. Continue only after retained effects/roots/hash equality and original anchor absence are authentic.

Resume only sequential existing miner after prior stopped. Restore/observe actual L1 controls, retain default freshness; while sequencer remains paused wait for rollback. Then allow empty checkpoints and drain normally to rebuild >=X; verify canonical X new hash, retained R same hash, and original proof still invalid. Do not assume fresh height alone is a new branch.

A hot read writes the repaired cache; cold reopen afterward cannot establish recovery from a stale persisted cache. Use one case hot-first and other close/reopen before any postfork read, or separately authenticated pre-fork caches. Capture exact before/after cache epoch/checkpoint/head and full snapshot equality in memory, without private values in reports.

Initialization case must keep original expectedRevision0; existing-head marker case keeps expectedRevision1. Capture retained snapshot separately from orphaned snapshot. Same marker throughBlockX now has new canonical hash and requires explicit newly reviewed marker context; never silently change business target/revision. New proof and beforeSubmit must enforce strict prior guards, unchanged paid-history and exclusive account lease.

Retain original included receipt/effect/cost as historical observation even after orphaning. Exclude it from current canonical fee total only after old effect noncanonical/absent, current receipt classification and synchronized exact FPC/private balance reconciliation agree. New fee counted exactly once after canonical replacement; no report overwrite of old paid evidence.

limits: No source edits, mining, reorg, SDK override, proof or service call executed.
Current hot/cold reader supports canonical-checkpoint mismatch reset, but this review does not prove real SDK cold backlog or native reorg recovery.
Journal3ff source approval alone does not supply application replacement/consent/history implementation.
An initialized-head marker test and initialization test are distinct; neither alone qualifies all replacement races or advanced-head recovery.
540s/4GiB, genuine-proof duration and cleanup reserve still need measured parent admission; do not start an infeasible scenario.
